sahneler.metin: In 1859, the most intense geomagnetic storm on record hit Earth.
Suddenly, telegraph stations sparked, and some caught fire.
Astronomer Richard Carrington had seen a brilliant flare on the Sun.
A burst of solar plasma reached Earth in less than a day.
It slammed into Earth's magnetic field.
Currents surged through long telegraph wires.
Auroras were so bright miners woke thinking it was morning.
Today, a storm this strong could damage power grids and satellites.

aciklama:
Carrington Event caused sparks and fires in telegraph stations worldwide. The cause: a geomagnetic storm inducing currents in long telegraph lines.
